instructions.text: Marinate pork slices in soy sauce, calamansi juice, banana ketchup, garlic, sugar, and pepper.
Skewer the marinated pork.
Prepare the grill.
Grill the pork skewers, basting with the marinade mixed with a little oil, for 5 minutes per side.
Ensure meat is fully cooked and slightly charred.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté garlic, onion, and ginger.
Add coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
Add the cleaned crabs into the pot.
Cover and cook until crabs turn orange.
Add spinach or malunggay leaves and cook.
Season with fish sauce.
Heat oil in a pan.
Sauté garlic and onion.
Add pork and cook until brown.
Pour tomato sauce and water. Let boil and simmer until pork is tender.
Add hotdogs, carrots, and potatoes. Cook.
Add bell peppers and cook.
Season with salt and pepper.
Prepare the pork: Cut 2 lbs (900 g) pork shoulder into 1.5-inch cubes. Rinse them under cold water, then pat dry with paper towels. Set aside in a bowl.

Slice 3 cloves of garlic (minced) and 1 medium onion (thinly sliced). Peel and slice 1 small carrot (optional) into 1-inch pieces. Chop 2 fresh bay leaves, 1 tablespoon fresh shrimp or fish sauce (optional for extra umami), and 2 small cloves of ginger (optional).

In a large, heavy-bottomed pan or pot, heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil over medium heat. Add the minced garlic, sliced onion, and julienned ginger if using. Sauté until aromatic and the onions turn translucent, about 2 minutes.

Push the aromatics to the sides and add the pork cubes in a single layer. Do not overcrowd; if the pan is small, do it in batches. Let the meat sear undisturbed for 3 minutes, then turn the pieces and continue browning until all sides have a nice brown crust.
Transfer the browned pork to a measuring cup or bowl, set aside. Pour 1 tablespoon of tomato sauce into the pan, scraping up all the browned bits (fond). This will add sweetness and depth of flavor.

Deglaze the pan with 1/2 cup of water, then return the pork to the pot. Sprinkle in 1/4 cup of dark soy sauce, 3 tablespoons of brown sugar (or 2 tablespoons of cane sugar if preferred), 2 teaspoons of fish sauce (if using), and 2 bay leaves. Stir to coat the pork evenly.

Add 1 cup of water (or enough to cover the pork by about 1 inch). Stir in a pinch of ground black pepper and 1 tablespoon of vinegar (optional for a slight tang). Bring the liquid to a gentle boil over medium-high heat.

Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer. Tight, slow cooking will break down the collagen and thicken the sauce. Let it continue to simmer for 60 minutes (3600 seconds), checking every 15 minutes to stir and prevent sticking. After about 45 minutes, you can add the optional carrot pieces if using, as they need a shorter cook time to stay crisp.
After 60 minutes, test the pork for tenderness; it should be fall‑apart and easy to shred. If not yet tender, cover and simmer for an additional 15–20 minutes, checking frequently.
Once the pork reaches the desired tenderness, taste the sauce and season to your liking. If the sauce is too thick, add a splash of water; if too thin, uncover for another 5 minutes to reduce.
Remove the pot from heat, transfer the pork and sauce to a serving dish, and garnish with chopped scallions or fried garlic if desired. Serve hot with steamed white rice.

Gather all ingredients: 1 lb ground pork, 1 cup pre-cooked rice (fried or just regular, with a little soy sauce added), 4 strips cooked ham or bacon, 1/2 cup diced carrots, 1/2 cup diced bell pepper, 1/2 cup frozen peas, 1/4 cup diced pimiento, 3 eggs, 1 tbsp vegetable oil, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp black pepper, 1/2 tsp paprika, 1 tsp dried oregano, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp brown sugar, 1/2 cup milk, 1/4 cup cream cheese, 2 tbsp chopped scallions, and 1 sheet of aluminum foil.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large sauté pan over medium heat. Add 3 cloves minced garlic and sauté until aromatic and lightly golden, about 1 minute.
Add the ground pork to the pan. Cook, stirring frequently, until the meat is browned and no longer pink, about 3 minutes.
Add the diced carrots, bell pepper, peas, and pimiento to the pan. Cook for 2 additional minutes, letting the veggies soften slightly.
Whisk the eggs with 1/4 cup milk and a pinch of salt, then pour the mixture over the pork and vegetables. Stir continuously until the eggs scramble and incorporate into the meat, about 2 minutes.

Shred the diced ham or bacon and fold into the pork mixture. Add the pre‑cooked rice, chopped scallions, soy sauce, fish sauce, paprika, oregano, salt, black pepper, and brown sugar. Stir until well combined.
Smooth the mixture into a loaf shape in your hand, then wrap it tightly in a sheet of aluminum foil to form a neat cylinder. Secure with kitchen twine or a second sheet of foil if needed.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Place the wrapped embutido in a baking dish or on a silicone mat.
Bake the embutido for 30 minutes. After 15 minutes, flip the wrap over to ensure even browning if you wish, but it’s optional.
Remove from the oven and carefully unwrap the foil. Slice the embutido into 1/2‑inch thick rounds.
Serve the slices hot, optionally with a drizzle of soy sauce or a light tomato sauce. Enjoy your homemade pork embutido!
Heat a pan with water and a little oil. Add hotdogs and cook until water evaporates and hotdogs are lightly fried.
In a separate pan, heat oil and fry garlic until golden. Add leftover rice and toss well to make sinangag (garlic rice).
Fry an egg sunny-side up.
Serve hotdogs, garlic rice, and fried egg together.
Boil water in a pot with tomatoes and onions.
Add the fish slices and simmer gently.
Add sinigang mix, radish, and string beans. Cook until tender.
Add water spinach (kangkong) and green chili. Turn off heat and cover.
Boil minced pork lungs and heart in water with lemongrass and pandan to remove odor.
Heat oil, saute garlic and onions until fragrant.
Add the boiled lungs and heart, cook for a few minutes.
Pour in vinegar, let it boil without stirring.
Add annatto water, carrots, radish, and chili. Simmer until dry.
Sauté garlic and onion in oil.
Add ground pork and cook until browned.
Pour in coconut milk and vinegar, let boil without stirring.
Add the prepared banana blossoms (puso ng saging) and simmer until tender.
Season with salt and pepper.
Place pork hock in a pot with water, soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, and peppercorns.
Bring to a boil, then simmer until pork is very tender.
Add dried banana blossoms and brown sugar.
Simmer until the sauce thickens slightly.

recipes.name: Pork Humba
recipes.description: A classic Filipino braised pork dish that balances sweet, sour, and umami flavors. The pork belly absorbs the sauce made from soy sauce, vinegar, brown sugar, and aromatic herbs, resulting in tender meat with a glossy glaze.

instructions.text: Heat oil in a cooking pot.
Sear the pork belly pieces until brown.
Add onion and garlic, saute until onion softens.
Pour soy sauce, vinegar, and water. Bring to a boil.
Add banana blossoms, salted black beans, and brown sugar. Simmer until pork is tender.
Boil water used for washing rice with ginger, tomatoes, and lemongrass.
Add squash and taro, cook until tender.
Add string beans, eggplant, and okra.
Season with bagoong isda and add malunggay leaves.
Marinate chicken in soy sauce and calamansi juice.
Pan-fry the chicken until lightly browned, then set aside.
Saute garlic and onions, add the marinade, tomato sauce, and chicken.
Add potatoes and simmer until the meat and potatoes are cooked.

recipes.name: Banana Cue
recipes.description: A classic Filipino street snack featuring deep‑fried saba bananas coated in caramelized sugar. Crispy on the outside, sweet and fragrant inside, often served skewered on small bamboo sticks or sticks of bamboo or plastic. Ideal for parties, fiestas, or a quick midnight munch.

instructions.text: Heat oil in a deep pan.
Fry the saba bananas for a few minutes.
Add brown sugar into the oil and let it caramelize and stick to the bananas.
Skewer the caramelized bananas on bamboo sticks.

recipes.name: Pork Igado
recipes.description: Igado is a hearty Filipino stew that originates from the Ilocano region, combining pork belly, pork liver, carrots, and green peas in a savory soy sauce base. It is known for its comforting flavor and convenient preparation, making it a staple in family meals.

instructions.text: Saute garlic and onions, then add pork tenderloin and cook until brown.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, and water. Simmer until meat is tender.
Add sliced pork liver and cook for a few minutes.
Stir in carrots, green peas, and bell peppers. Cook until vegetables are tender.
Saute garlic, onions, and diced pork until lightly browned.
Add pork liver and cook briefly.
Pour in tomato sauce and water, add bay leaves. Simmer until pork is tender.
Add potatoes, carrots, hotdogs, and raisins. Cook until potatoes are soft.
Marinate pork chops in soy sauce, calamansi, and garlic.
Heat oil in a pan.
Fry the marinated pork chops until golden brown.
In the same pan, fry the garlic rice.
Fry an egg sunny-side up.
Assemble pork, rice, and egg on a plate.

recipes.name: Sinigang na Alimango
recipes.description: A tangy, tomato-based crab soup flavored with tamarind broth, fresh vegetables, and a touch of heat—perfect for a comforting Filipino meal.

instructions.text: Boil water in a pot with tomatoes and onions.
Add tamarind mix and simmer.
Add the crabs and cook.
Add the vegetables (radish, string beans, eggplant) and cook.
Add kangkong (water spinach) and turn off heat.
Boil pork belly until tender, then chop into cubes.
Deep fry tofu until golden and crispy, then cut into cubes.
Mix soy sauce, vinegar, chopped onions, and chilies in a bowl.
Combine pork and tofu in a serving dish.
Pour the soy-vinegar dressing over the pork and tofu.
Marinate chicken pieces in vinegar, calamansi, lemongrass, garlic, and ginger.
Prepare the basting sauce with annatto oil and butter.
Grill the chicken over hot coals.
Baste frequently with the annatto oil mixture while grilling.
Grill until fully cooked.
Boil chicken breast until tender, then shred finely.
Sauté garlic, onions, and ginger in a pan.
Add the shredded chicken, soy sauce, and a little vinegar.
Cook until the chicken is relatively dry and toasted.
Serve over steamed rice wrapped in a banana leaf.
Sauté garlic until lightly browned.
Add shrimp paste (bagoong) and cook.
Add day-old rice, breaking up any lumps, and toss to coat.
Stir-fry until well combined and heated through.
Top with sliced green mangoes and scrambled eggs before serving.
Boil the goat innards with ginger to remove impurities, then slice into bite-sized pieces.
Sauté minced garlic, onion, and ginger in a pot.
Add the sliced innards and stir-fry.
Pour water, add the goat bile, and simmer until the meat is perfectly tender.
Marinate chicken in pineapple juice from the canned chunks.
Sauté garlic and onion, then pan-fry the marinated chicken until light brown.
Pour the marinade and evaporated milk. Let it simmer.
Add pineapple chunks, carrots, and bell peppers. Cook until vegetables are tender.
Pan-fry pork belly pieces in a wok until they start to render fat and turn brown.
Add minced garlic and sauté until fragrant.
Pour in soy sauce, vinegar, and a bit of water. Simmer covered.
Add string beans (sitaw) and cook until tender but still crisp.
Marinate thin slices of beef in soy sauce, garlic, sugar, and calamansi juice.
Pan-fry the beef tapa in a skillet until fully cooked and slightly caramelized.
Sauté garlic and cold rice to make sinangag.
Fry an egg and assemble the Tapsilog on a plate.

recipes.name: Adobong Kangkong
recipes.description: Water spinach cooked adobo-style in soy sauce, vinegar, and garlic.

instructions.text: Heat oil in a pan and saut� garlic until golden brown.
Add pork slices (optional) and cook until lightly browned.
Pour in soy sauce and vinegar. Let it boil without stirring.
Add the kangkong stems first and cook briefly.
Add the kangkong leaves, toss quickly until just wilted. Season with pepper.
Grill or pan-fry chicken thighs until fully cooked.
Chop the cooked chicken into very small pieces.
Melt butter in a pan, sauté onions, then add the chopped chicken.
Stir in mayonnaise, chicken liver, and chili peppers. Mix well and serve on a sizzling plate.
Heat oil in a pan.
Sauté garlic, onion, and tomatoes until softened.
Add the squid. Sauté for 2 minutes.
Pour in soy sauce and vinegar. Let it boil without stirring.
Stir and add water. Simmer for 3 minutes. Do not overcook the squid to keep it tender.
Season with salt, pepper, and sugar to taste.
In a large bowl, combine pork belly, soy sauce, calamansi juice, garlic, ketchup, salt, and pepper.
Massage the marinade into the meat and let it marinate for at least 3 hours.
Preheat the grill.
Grill the pork belly over hot coals for about 5 to 7 minutes per side, basting with the leftover marinade mixed with oil.
Slice into bite-sized pieces before serving.
Heat oil in a pan. Sauté garlic and onion.
Add pork and shrimp. Cook until the pork turns light brown.
Add the ubod (heart of palm), carrots, and green beans.
Pour a little water and simmer until the vegetables are tender. Season with fish sauce.
Let the filling cool.
Wrap the filling in a fresh lumpia wrapper with a leaf of lettuce.
Serve with a sweet peanut garlic sauce on top.
Drain the canned tuna chunks well.
Heat oil in a pan and lightly fry the tuna flakes until slightly crisp. Set aside.
In the same pan, melt butter and sauté chopped onions and ginger.
Add the fried tuna back into the pan. Stir well.
Mix in mayonnaise, soy sauce, and calamansi juice.
Add chopped chili peppers and season with salt and pepper.
Serve on a sizzling plate topped with an egg.

recipes.name: Adobong Mais
recipes.description: A beloved Filipino dish that transforms sweet corn into a savory, slightly tangy stew, perfect as a side or main dish with rice.

instructions.text: Heat oil in a pan. Sauté garlic and onions until softened.
Add ground pork and cook until browned.
Add the scraped corn kernels. Stir to combine.
Pour in soy sauce, vinegar, and a little water. Let it boil.
Lower the heat and simmer until the corn is tender and the liquid has reduced.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

recipes.name: Halabos Alimango
recipes.description: Steamed mud crabs cooked simply in their own juices with a little salt and lemon-lime soda.

instructions.text: Clean the live crabs thoroughly. Tie the claws if not already tied.
Place the crabs in a large pot. Add salt and pour lemon-lime soda (Sprite or 7-Up) to half-cover them.
Cover the pot and cook on high heat until the crabs turn bright orange.
Remove the lid, flip the crabs, and cook for a few more minutes to reduce the liquid.
Serve with a garlic butter or vinegar dipping sauce.
Boil pork face (maskara) and ears until tender, then grill until slightly charred.
Chop the grilled pork into small pieces.
Saute onions, garlic, and chopped pork in a pan.
Add chicken liver, soy sauce, calamansi juice, and chili. Mix well.
Serve on a hot sizzling plate with an egg on top.
Fry the whole fish until crispy and golden brown, then set aside.
Sauté garlic, onions, and bell peppers in a pan.
Add pineapple chunks, vinegar, ketchup, sugar, and soy sauce.
Simmer until the sauce thickens.
Pour the sweet and sour sauce over the fried fish.

recipes.name: Ginataang Tuna
recipes.description: A comforting Filipino stew with silky coconut milk, tender pieces of fresh tuna, and a medley of starchy vegetables, all seasoned with garlic, ginger, and a hint of fish sauce for a savory depth.

instructions.text: Heat oil in a pan. Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle boil.
Add the tuna chunks and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add sliced eggplant, string beans, and green chilies.
Season with fish sauce and pepper. Simmer until the vegetables are cooked and the sauce reduces.
Clean and slice the fish (preferably bangus or tilapia) into 1‑in. thick fillets, pat dry with paper towels.
In a bowl, season the fish with 2 Tbsp. fish sauce, juice of 1 calamansi, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp white pepper. Let it marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat 2 Tbsp. vegetable oil in a large heavy‑bottomed skillet over medium heat.
Add 4 cloves of sliced garlic and cook until golden brown, about 15 seconds.
Stir in 1 medium sliced onion and sauté until translucent, about 45 seconds.
Add 1 tsp. minced ginger and 1 sliced red chili. Cook for 10 seconds until fragrant.
Place the marinated fish pieces into the skillet, searing each side for about 30 seconds.
Pour in 1 cup of coconut milk, then add 1 Tbsp. fish sauce + 1 tsp. brown sugar to balance the flavors.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and let the mixture simmer gently for 180 seconds (3 minutes) until the fish is opaque and cooked through.
Uncover, stir in the juice of 1/2 calamansi, and let it finish cooking for an additional 30 seconds.
Adjust seasoning with a pinch of salt if needed. Remove from heat.
Garnish with chopped scallions and cilantro, then serve hot over steamed rice.

Gather your ingredients: pre‑cooked or day‑old rice (about 2 cups), 6 cloves of garlic, 2 tablespoons of cooking oil (vegetable, coconut or olive), a pinch of salt for seasoning, and optional tools such as a large non‑stick skillet, a wooden spoon or spatula.

Wash your hands and prepare your workspace. Lay out the rice in a shallow bowl so you can easily break up the clumps. – Optional but recommended: refrigerate the rice for 30 minutes to take the moisture out of it; this improves the texture of the sinangag.
Slice or finely mince the garlic cloves. A good rule of thumb is about 6 cloves for 2 cups of rice. If you prefer a milder aroma, claw the cloves a bit thinner.

Heat the 2 tablespoons of oil in a large non‑stick skillet over medium‑high heat. _(Tip: The skillet should be hot enough that a single drop of water reacts with a wisp of steam, but not so hot that it scorches.)_

Add the minced garlic to the pan and let it sizzle. Cook until the garlic turns a light golden brown and releases a fragrant aroma. This should take about 60 seconds; keep an eye on it so it doesn’t burn.
Pour the pre‑cooked rice into the skillet. Use the back of the spoon to distribute the rice evenly across the surface of the pan. The rice should sizzle gently as it hits the hot oil.
Using a spatula, break up any clumps of rice. Press the rice down lightly and let it sit without stirring for the first 30 seconds; this promotes even searing.

Stir the rice continuously for 60 seconds, making sure the heat stays medium‑high so the rice heats through quickly but doesn’t stick to the bottom. The goal is a slightly crisp crust at the bottom while keeping the interior moist.
Season with a pinch of fine sea salt or kosher salt to taste. Stir in the salt and let it settle for 5 seconds to let the flavors meld.

Once the rice reaches a fragrant, lightly caramelized texture on the outer layer and is heated through, transfer it to a serving plate or bowl. If you’re preparing multiple orders, cover the bowl with foil to keep the rice warm while you refresh the pan for the next batch.
Heat oil in a pan.
Sauté garlic, onion, and tomatoes.
Add ground pork and cook until brown.
Add water, cover, and let boil.
Add upo (bottle gourd) slices and cook until tender.
Season with fish sauce and pepper.
Clean the bangus (milkfish) by opening the belly, removing the gills, rinsing under cold water, and patting dry with a clean towel.

Gather the sauce ingredients: 4 cups of water, 1 cup of vinegar (preferably palm vinegar for authenticity), 2 bay leaves, 1 teaspoon of whole peppercorns, 1 teaspoon of salt, 1 teaspoon of sugar, and 1 medium onion sliced, 4 cloves of garlic minced, and 2 tablespoons of oil.
In a mixing bowl, combine the water, vinegar, bay leaves, peppercorns, salt, and sugar; stir until the sugar dissolves. Set aside.
Heat the oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and sliced onion, sautéing until they turn golden brown and fragrant.

Add the cleaned bangus pieces to the pan, gently placing them in the oil. Seared each side for about 2 minutes on the first side and an additional 2 minutes on the second side until the fish is lightly browned.
Pour the pre-mixed sauce into the pan, carefully submerging the fish. Reduce the heat and allow the mixture to come to a gentle boil.
Once boiling, lower the heat to a simmer and cook uncovered for 30 minutes, allowing the fish to absorb the flavors and the sauce to thicken slightly.

Check the fish for doneness; a perfectly cooked bangus Paksiw will be opaque and flake easily when tested with a fork. If the sauce is too acidic, add a pinch more sugar or a splash of water to balance.
Turn off the heat, transfer the bangus Paksiw to a serving dish, and garnish with sliced scallions or a few chili flakes if desired. Serve hot with steamed white rice.

Dice 500 g pork belly into 1‑inch cubes and 200 g pork liver or heart into 1‑inch cubes. If using fresh pork blood, strain it through a cheesecloth to remove clumps; set aside 200 ml separate from the meat.
Heat 4 Tbsp coconut oil in a double‑bottomed pot over medium heat. Add 6 minced garlic cloves and sauté for 1 min until fragrant.
Add a finely chopped 1 medium onion and sauté until translucent, about 3 min.
Stir in 2 diced tomatoes and cook for 2 min until they soften.
Pour in 2 Tbsp shrimp paste (patis) and sauté for another 30 s until it blends with the aromatics.
Add the diced pork pieces to the pot, stirring to coat them in the oil and aromatics. Sear until the pork is lightly browned on all sides, about 5 min.
Pour 2 cups of sanitod (pork stock) and 1 cup of vinegar, then add 2 bay leaves, 1 tsp ground black pepper, and 1 tsp salt. Bring the mixture to a brisk boil.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let the pork simmer gently for 20 min to allow the flavors to meld.
Stir in the strained pork blood slowly, then add 1 cup of water (or more if you prefer a thinner sauce). Keep the heat low.
Continue simmering uncovered for another 15 min, removing any foam that rises, until the sauce thickens and the pork is tender.
Taste and adjust seasoning with extra salt, pepper, or vinegar if needed. If the sauce is too thick, add a splash of water; if too thin, let it reduce for an additional 5 min.
Plate the dinuguan hot, garnish with chopped spring onions or fried garlic if desired, and serve with steamed rice or boiled plantains.
Trim the milkfish (bangus) and pat it dry, then cut into bite‑sized strips. Set aside.

In a small bowl, whisk together calamansi juice, white pepper, a pinch of salt, and a splash of soy sauce. Toss the milkfish strips in this mixture to marinate for 60 seconds, then leave aside for 30 seconds to rest.

Heat 3 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium heat. Add 2 cloves of minced garlic and 1 thinly sliced onion; sauté until the garlic is fragrant and the onion turns translucent, about 60 seconds.
Add 1 cup of cherry tomatoes, quartered, and cook for another 30 seconds until they start to soften.
Fold in the marinated milkfish strips and stir‑fry until the flesh turns slightly opaque and begins to brown, about 120 seconds.
Pour in 1 tablespoon of soy sauce, 2 teaspoons of fermented shrimp paste (bagoong), and 1 teaspoon of fish sauce. Stir to coat the fish and let it caramelize for 60 seconds.
Add 1 tablespoon of vinegar and a pinch of sugar to balance acidity. Stir briefly for 30 seconds.
Pour in 1 cup of water, bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to a simmer. Let it cook for 300 seconds to allow the flavors to meld and the liquid to thicken slightly.
Stir in 1 cooked hard‑boiled egg, crumbled, and cook together for 60 seconds to warm the egg and meld it with the mixture.
Finely dice 1 small bell pepper (red or green) and 1 small carrot. Add them to the wok and sauté for 90 seconds until just tender.
Sprinkle in 1 tablespoon of freshly chopped parsley, 1 teaspoon of chopped scallions, and 1 teaspoon of dried oregano. Combine for 30 seconds.
Season the sisig with pepper, a pinch of salt, and a dash of hot sauce if you like it spicier. Stir for 30 seconds.
Lower the heat, cover the wok, and let the sisig rest for 60 seconds to allow steam to finish cooking the vegetables.
Serve the Bangus Sisig on a hot plate or platter, topped with a thin slice of fresh cucumber, a drizzle of soy sauce, and an extra sprinkle of parsley. Garnish with a few chili flakes if desired.
Drain the tilapia fillets and pat them dry. Set aside.

Heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a medium-sized pot over medium heat. Add 4 cloves of minced garlic, 1 diced onion, and 1 thumb‑size piece of grated ginger. Sauté until the aromatics are fragrant and the onions turn translucent, about 90 seconds.
Add 2 diced medium tomatoes to the pot. Cook until the tomatoes soften and break down, about 120 seconds.
Pour in one cup of coconut milk (the can’s whole milk or coconut cream works best). Bring the mixture to a gentle boil, then lower the heat and let it simmer for 60 seconds before adding the fish.
Gently nestle the tilapia fillets into the coconut milk. Cover the pot and simmer on low heat for 180 seconds (about 3 minutes) or until the fish flakes easily with a fork.
Stir in 1 tablespoon of fish sauce, a pinch of sugar, and a handful of sliced green chili peppers (adjust to taste). Let the flavors meld for 30 seconds.
Remove the pot from heat, squeeze fresh calamansi or lime juice over the dish, season with salt and pepper to taste, and serve hot with steamed rice.
Shave the fresh tuna into thin, bite‑size strips using a sharp, clean knife. The tuna should be filleted from the belly and rib, then sliced so each strip is about 1.5–2 cm wide for even marinating.
In a bowl, whisk together 2 tablespoons of white wine vinegar, 1 tablespoon of calamansi or lime juice, and 1/4 teaspoon of salt until the salt dissolves.

Add the sliced tuna to the vinegar mixture. Gently toss to coat every piece, then pour 1 tablespoon of sliced onion (white or red for color), 1 tablespoon of diced cucumber, and 1 tablespoon of chopped fresh cilantro into the bowl.
Fold in 2 teaspoons of minced garlic and 1/4 teaspoon of turmeric powder for a subtle color and aroma. Mix quickly and then cover the bowl with plastic wrap.
Place the bowl in the refrigerator for 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld while the tuna firms slightly.
Before serving, taste the kinilaw and adjust seasoning with extra salt or a splash of calamansi if needed. Garnish with extra cilantro or thinly sliced green onions.
Serve the kinilaw immediately over a bed of sliced banana leaves or as a Filipino-style ceviche on warm rice cakes or crispy tortilla chips for a delightful starter.
Pan-fry potatoes and carrots, set aside.
In the same pan, sauté garlic, onion, and ginger.
Add chicken pieces and cook until lightly browned.
Add curry powder and fish sauce.
Pour coconut milk and water, simmer until chicken is tender.
Return potatoes, carrots, and add bell peppers. Simmer.
Coat pork pieces in cornstarch.
Deep fry pork until golden brown and crispy, then set aside.
In a separate pan, sauté garlic, onion, and bell peppers.
Add pineapple chunks and cook.
Pour in the sweet and sour sauce (vinegar, ketchup, sugar, soy sauce, cornstarch slurry).
Cook until sauce thickens.
Toss in the fried pork until coated.
Marinate bangus in vinegar, crushed garlic, peppercorn, and salt.
Heat oil in a frying pan.
Fry the marinated bangus skin-side down first until golden brown.
Flip and fry the other side until crispy and cooked through.
Mix ground pork, minced carrots, onion, garlic, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Place a spoonful of the mixture on a lumpia wrapper and roll tightly.
Heat oil in a deep pan.
Deep fry the rolls until golden brown and crispy.
Drain excess oil on paper towels.
Sauté garlic and onion in oil.
Add sliced pork and cook until brown.
Pour in coconut milk and let boil.
Add unripe jackfruit (langka) and simmer until tender.
Add chili peppers and shrimp paste (bagoong) to taste, cook.
Boil beef shank with onions, lemongrass, and peppercorns until very tender.
Add batwan or sinigang mix for sourness.
Add annatto water (atsuete) for color.
Add green jackfruit and cook until tender.
Add chili peppers and season with fish sauce.
Sauté garlic, onion, and tomatoes in a pan.
Add beaten eggs and scramble until slightly set, then remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add ampalaya (bitter gourd) and cook for a few minutes until tender but crisp.
Return the eggs to the pan, season with salt and pepper, and toss.
Boil pork hocks or belly until tender.
Add batwan or sinigang mix and soaked kadyos beans. Simmer until beans are soft.
Add jackfruit (langka) and cook until tender.
Season with salt and add sweet potato tops.
Sauté garlic and onion in a pan.
Add pork slices and cook until browned.
Add water and simmer until pork is tender.
Add sliced patola (sponge gourd) and cook until soft.
Season with fish sauce and pepper.
Sauté garlic and onion in oil.
Add sliced pork or tinapa flakes and cook for a few minutes.
Add pechay stalks and cook.
Add pechay leaves and cook until wilted.
Season with oyster sauce or salt.
Boil water in a large pot with onions and peppercorns.
Add pork belly or ribs and simmer until tender.
Add saba bananas and potatoes, cook until soft.
Add cabbage and pechay, turn off heat and let sit.
Soak bihon noodles in water to soften.
Saute garlic, onions, pork, and chicken in a large pan or wok.
Add soy sauce, chicken broth, carrots, and cabbage. Bring to a boil.
Toss in the soaked noodles and stir-fry until liquid is absorbed.

recipes.name: Pancit Canton
recipes.description: A savory stir‑fried noodle dish featuring a blend of pork, shrimp, and fresh vegetables, seasoned with soy and fish sauce.

instructions.text: Saute garlic, onions, and sliced pork until browned.
Add shrimp, snow peas, carrots, and cabbage. Cook briefly and set aside.
In the same pan, boil chicken broth and soy sauce.
Add the pancit canton noodles and cook until liquid is absorbed. Mix in the vegetables and meat.
Prepare the filling by sautéing garlic, onion, ground pork, carrots, potatoes, and raisins. Cook until tender and set aside to cool.
Prepare the dough by cutting butter into flour and sugar, then slowly adding cold water. Knead and rest.
Flatten the dough and cut into circles.
Place filling in the center, fold, and seal the edges.
Deep fry or bake until golden brown.
Soak glass noodles in water.
Sauté garlic and onions in a pan.
Add chicken and cook until brown.
Add carrots, cabbage, and soy sauce, stirring well.
Add soaked noodles and chicken broth, simmering until liquid is absorbed.
Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger in a pot.
Add shrimp and cook until pink.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a boil.
Add squash and cook until tender.
Add string beans and cook.
Sauté garlic and onions in a pot.
Add pork slices and cook until browned.
Add chicken broth and bring to a simmer.
Add grated fresh corn and cook.
Add spinach leaves and season with fish sauce.
Fry tofu cubes until crispy, then set aside.
Sauté onions and garlic in a pan.
Add mayonnaise, soy sauce, and calamansi juice to the pan.
Toss in the crispy tofu and chopped green chilies.
Serve on a sizzling plate.
Marinate chicken in soy sauce, garlic, and peppercorns.
Pan-fry chicken pieces until browned.
Pour in the marinade, add water and vinegar. Bring to a boil.
Simmer on low heat until chicken is tender and sauce thickens.
Saute garlic and onions, then brown the chicken pieces.
Add tomato sauce, water, and dried bay leaves. Simmer until chicken is half-cooked.
Add potatoes, carrots, and hotdogs. Cook until tender.
Stir in bell peppers and green peas. Season with salt and pepper.
Saute garlic, onions, and tomatoes in a pan.
Add ground pork or shrimp and cook until lightly browned.
Add sliced chayote (sayote) and stir-fry.
Pour a little water and simmer until the sayote is tender but crisp.
Boil pork belly with garlic, peppercorns, and bay leaves until tender.
Remove from water and let it cool completely (air dry for crispiness).
Deep fry the pork belly in hot oil until golden brown and crispy.
Chop into bite-sized pieces and serve with lechon sauce.
Beat eggs in a bowl with salt and pepper.
Sauté chopped onions and tomatoes in a pan.
Pour the beaten eggs into the pan.
Cook until the bottom is set, then flip to cook the other side.
Serve warm.
Marinate chicken in soy sauce, garlic, and vinegar.
Pan-fry chicken pieces until brown on both sides.
Pour the marinade and water into the pan and bring to a boil.
Simmer until chicken is tender.
Add peppercorns and bay leaves, and simmer until sauce thickens.
Boil chicken bones and meat with onions and celery to make broth.
Shred the cooked chicken meat.
Boil fresh egg noodles until tender, then place in a bowl.
Top noodles with shredded chicken, boiled egg, and toasted garlic.
Pour the hot chicken broth over the noodles and serve.
Sauté garlic and onions, then brown the chicken pieces.
Add chorizo de bilbao and tomato sauce, and simmer.
Pour in water and simmer until chicken is tender.
Add potatoes, saba bananas, and chick peas, cooking.
Add pechay and cabbage, cooking.
Sauté garlic and onions in a pan.
Add small shrimp and pork strips, cooking until browned.
Add carrots and tofu cubes, cooking.
Toss in the mung bean sprouts (togue).
Season with soy sauce and cook.
Soak bihon noodles in water until soft.
Boil pork in water until tender, then slice into strips.
Prepare the sauce by mixing shrimp juice, annatto water, and pork broth in a pot. Simmer until thick.
Assemble the noodles, pour the sauce, and top with crushed chicharon, boiled eggs, and tinapa flakes.
Roll saba banana slices and jackfruit strips in brown sugar.
Wrap the sugared banana and jackfruit in spring roll wrappers.
Heat oil in a pan, add more brown sugar to caramelize, and fry the wrapped bananas until golden and crisp.
Boil beef brisket with star anise and ginger until very tender.
Sauté garlic, ginger, and onion in a separate pan.
Add the boiled beef, soy sauce, sugar, and some of the beef stock. Simmer until the sauce thickens.
Serve with garlic fried rice and a bowl of the remaining clear beef broth.
Sauté pork belly until brown and oil is extracted.
Add onion, garlic, and shrimp paste (bagoong alamang). Cook for a few minutes.
Add squash and water, cover, and simmer until squash is semi-soft.
Add string beans, eggplant, bitter melon (ampalaya), and okra. Cook until vegetables are tender.
Sauté garlic and onion in a pan.
Add ground pork and cook until nicely browned.
Pour tomato sauce and a little water, then simmer.
Add diced potatoes, carrots, and raisins. Cook until potatoes are soft.
Boil water in a pot. Add pork belly, tomatoes, and onion, simmering until pork is tender.
Add taro (gabi) and continue to boil until the broth thickens slightly.
Stir in the tamarind soup base (sinigang mix).
Add string beans, eggplant, daikon radish, and kangkong (water spinach).
Deep-fry the marinated chicken leg or thigh until golden brown and cooked through.
Sauté leftover rice with lots of minced garlic to make sinangag.
Fry a sunny-side-up egg.
Plate the fried chicken, garlic rice, and egg together.
Marinate milkfish (bangus) in vinegar, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Pan-fry the marinated milkfish until the skin is crispy and golden brown.
Cook garlic fried rice (sinangag) in a separate pan.
Fry a sunny-side-up egg and serve with the fish and rice.
Marinate beef cubes in soy sauce, oyster sauce, and minced garlic.
Fry lots of minced garlic in butter and olive oil until crispy, then set aside.
In the same pan, sear the marinated beef over high heat until cooked to your preference.
Toss the beef with the toasted garlic before serving.
Heat oil in a pan or wok.
Sauté garlic and onion until onion becomes soft.
Add the sliced pork. Cook until the color turns light brown.
Pour water and boil. Let it simmer until pork is tender.
Add the shrimp and cook for 2 minutes.
Put-in the oyster sauce and Knorr Shrimp Cube. Stir.
Add the cauliflower, carrots, bell pepper, and snow peas. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add the cabbage and quail eggs. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour-in the dissolved cornstarch. Stir until sauce thickens.
Grill the eggplants until the skin is charred and the inside is soft.
Let the eggplants cool, then peel off the skin, keeping the crown intact.
Flatten the peeled eggplants using a fork.
Beat eggs in a wide bowl and season with salt and pepper.
Dip the flattened eggplants into the beaten egg mixture.
Heat oil in a pan. Fry the eggplants until golden brown on both sides.
Heat oil in a pan.
Sauté garlic, onion, and tomatoes until soft.
Add pork pieces and cook until light brown.
Add water and simmer until pork is tender.
Add squash and string beans. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add the remaining vegetables like eggplant and bitter gourd. Cook for another 3 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and pepper.
Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger in a pot.
Add water and bring to a boil.
Add green papaya wedges and simmer.
Add the fish slices and cook.
Add malunggay leaves, season with fish sauce, and serve.
Clean the bangus, keeping the scales on. Split it open from the back and remove the innards.
In a bowl, mix chopped tomatoes, onions, ginger, and calamansi juice. Season with salt and pepper.
Stuff the bangus with the tomato and onion mixture.
Wrap the stuffed bangus tightly in aluminum foil or banana leaves.
Grill over hot coals for 15 to 20 minutes per side.
Clean the squid thoroughly and remove the ink sac and the plastic-like pen.
Mix chopped tomatoes, onions, and ginger. Season with salt.
Stuff the squid with the tomato mixture and secure the ends with toothpicks.
Combine soy sauce, calamansi juice, and oil for the marinade and basting sauce.
Grill the stuffed squid for 2 to 3 minutes per side. Do not overcook.
Heat oil in a cooking pot. Sauté garlic and onion.
Add sliced pork and cook until browned.
Add kikiam and fish balls. Stir and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Add the fresh miki noodles and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the dissolved cornstarch to thicken the soup.
Slowly pour in beaten eggs while stirring continuously.
Season with salt, pepper, and a bit of soy sauce.
Heat oil and sauté garlic and onion.
Add sweet potato and tofu. Cook for 3 minutes.
Add green beans and carrots. Stir and cook for another 3 minutes.
Add cabbage and bean sprouts. Season with salt and pepper. Cook for 2 minutes.
Let the vegetable filling cool completely and drain any excess liquid.
Place a spoonful of filling on a lumpia wrapper, roll tightly, and seal the edges with water.
Deep fry the lumpia until golden brown and crispy.
Scrape the meat of the bangus (milkfish) while keeping the skin and head intact.
Marinate the skin in soy sauce and calamansi juice.
Boil the fish meat for 5 minutes, drain, and remove the bones.
Sauté garlic, onion, and tomatoes. Add the fish meat, carrots, peas, and raisins. Cook for 5 minutes.
Season with salt, pepper, and oyster sauce. Let the mixture cool.
Mix raw eggs into the cooked fish mixture.
Stuff the mixture back into the marinated bangus skin.
Fry the stuffed bangus until golden brown and crispy.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a large pot over medium heat. No cooking time is needed for this step.
Add 4 cloves of minced garlic and sauté until fragrant and lightly golden, about 1 minute.
Add 500 g of peeled and deveined shrimp, stirring until they turn opaque and just pink, roughly 2 minutes.
Add 2 medium diced tomatoes and sauté until the tomatoes soften, around 1 minute.
Pour in 4 cups of water, then add the tamarind base (or a commercial sinigang mix) to the pot and stir to combine.
Bring the liquid to a gentle boil, then reduce the heat to a low simmer and let the broth cook for 10 minutes to develop flavor.
Add 1 cup sliced onion, 1 cup cubed eggplant, 1 cup sliced okra, 1 cup sliced bitter melon, and 1 cup cut long beans. Stir gently.
Continue simmering until the vegetables are crisp-tender and the shrimp remain just cooked, about 5 minutes.
Season with fish sauce, a dash of pepper, and additional tamarind base if desired. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Turn off the heat and serve the Shrimp Sinigang hot, accompanied by steamed rice.

Gather all ingredients: 1 whole chicken, 1 cup chopped tomatoes, 1 cup string beans cut into 2‑inch pieces, 1 cup okra pods, 1/2 cup kangkong leaves, 1 medium onion chopped, 3 cloves garlic minced, 1 thumb-sized ginger sliced, 2 tbsp fish sauce (patis), 1 tbsp calamansi lime juice, 2 tbsp shrimp paste (optional), 2 cups water, salt to taste, oil for cooking.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large pot over medium heat. Once hot, add the minced garlic and sauté until fragrant and golden, about 1 minute.
Add the chopped onion to the pot. Sauté until translucent, about 1½ minutes.
Stir in the sliced ginger and cook for another minute until the aroma is released.
Add the diced tomatoes and cook, stirring frequently, until they start to break down and soften, about 2 minutes.
Introduce the chicken pieces to the pot. Stir them into the aromatics, turning to coat and lightly brown on all sides, roughly 3 minutes.
Pour in 2 cups of water and bring the mixture to a gentle boil. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and let it simmer for 10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld and the chicken to cook through.
Uncover the pot and stir in the fish sauce and calamansi juice. Taste and adjust with more fish sauce or a pinch of salt if needed.
Add the string beans and okra pods to the pot. Cook for an additional 3 minutes or until the vegetables are tender but still crisp.
Finally, pour in the kangkong leaves and simmer for 1 minute until just wilted.
Remove from heat, serve hot over steamed rice, and enjoy your authentic Sinampalukang Manok!
Heat a cooking pot and add pork belly. Sear until lightly browned.
Add water, tomatoes, and onions. Bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer until the pork is tender, about 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Add the taro (gabi) and simmer for another 10 minutes to thicken the soup.
Stir in the sinigang mix (tamarind soup base).
Add string beans, radish, and eggplant. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the water spinach (kangkong) and green chilies. Turn off the heat and cover for 2 minutes.
Boil beef shanks with bone marrow and onions in a large pot.
Skim the scum and simmer on low heat until the meat falls off the bone.
Add corn on the cob and cook until tender.
Add pechay and cabbage. Turn off heat and cover.

recipes.name: Tortang Giniling
recipes.description: Filipino ground pork omelet mixed with vegetables, pan-fried until golden.

instructions.text: Saut� garlic and onion in oil until soft.
Add the ground pork and cook until browned, breaking it apart.
Add diced carrots, green peas, and raisins. Cook until carrots soften.
Season with soy sauce, salt, and pepper. Set the cooked meat aside to cool slightly.
Beat eggs in a bowl and mix in the cooked ground pork filling.
Heat oil in a pan, pour the egg-meat mixture, and pan-fry until golden brown on both sides.
Sauté garlic and onions, then add beef chunks and brown them.
Add tomato sauce, water, and liver spread. Simmer until the beef is very tender.
Add potatoes and carrots, cooking until soft.
Add bell peppers and green olives, simmer briefly before serving.
Boil beef oxtail and tripe in a large pot with water until extremely tender.
Toast ground rice and peanuts in a pan, then set aside.
Sauté annatto seeds in oil, discard seeds, then use the oil to sauté garlic and onions. Add the meat, peanut butter, and toasted rice to the broth.
Blanch the string beans, eggplant, banana blossom, and bok choy separately, then add to the stew.
Pan-fry beef chunks in a pot until brown on all sides.
Add garlic and onion, then pour in tomato sauce, soy sauce, and beef broth. Cover and simmer until tender.
Add potatoes and cook until soft.
Stir in bell peppers and cook for a few more minutes.

recipes.name: Beef Steak
recipes.description: Filipino beef steak marinated in soy sauce and calamansi, topped with onion rings.

instructions.text: Marinate beef slices in soy sauce, calamansi juice, and ground pepper for at least 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan and pan-fry the marinated beef until brown on both sides. Set aside.
In the same pan, saut� onion rings until slightly softened. Set aside.
Pour the remaining marinade into the pan, add a little water, and bring to a boil.
Return the beef to the pan and simmer until tender and sauce reduces.
Top with the saut�ed onion rings and serve.
In a bowl, combine beef, soy sauce, garlic, sugar, and pepper. Marinate.
Heat a pan and place the marinated beef with its liquid.
Cook until liquid evaporates and oil from the beef comes out.
Fry the beef in its own oil or add a little cooking oil until browned.

recipes.name: Bicol Express
recipes.description: Spicy pork stew cooked in coconut milk and shrimp paste with lots of chilies.

instructions.text: Heat oil and saut� garlic, onion, and ginger until fragrant.
Add pork belly strips and cook until edges are lightly browned.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a boil, stirring occasionally.
Add shrimp paste (bagoong alamang) and stir well.
Add long green chili peppers and simmer until the pork is tender and the sauce thickens.
Add coconut cream and simmer until oil separates from the sauce.

Gather all ingredients: 500 g pork loin or sirloin cut into ½‑inch thick strips, ¼ cup soy sauce, 2 Tbsp calamansi juice (or lemon juice if unavailable), 2 crushed garlic cloves, 1 tsp freshly ground black pepper, 1 bay leaf, 1 medium red onion sliced into wedges, 2 Tbsp cooking oil, 1 Tbsp brown sugar (optional).

In a medium bowl whisk together soy sauce, calamansi juice, crushed garlic, pepper, and the bay leaf until well blended. Coat the pork strips in this mixture, cover, and let marinate for at least 10 minutes to absorb the flavors.
Heat 2 Tbsp oil in a large skillet or wok over medium‑high heat. Add the minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds, just until fragrant and slightly golden.

Add the marinated pork strips in a single layer, letting the sides sear for about 60 seconds each. The pork should develop a light brown crust; do not overcrowd the pan. Return the bay leaf to the pan.
Push the pork to the sides of the skillet and add the sliced onion wedges. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the onions become translucent and start to caramelize, about 180 seconds.

Pour the remaining marinating sauce over the pork and onions. Stir to coat everything evenly, then reduce the heat to medium and let the mixture come to a light simmer. Allow it to simmer undisturbed for about 300 seconds so the pork tenderizes and absorbs the sauce.
If desired, add 1 Tbsp brown sugar to balance the acidity, stir until dissolved, and simmer for an additional 120 seconds. The sauce should thicken slightly.

Remove the skillet from heat. Let the Bistek Baboy rest in the pan for 120 seconds to allow the flavors to meld further. Serve hot over steamed rice, spooning generous amounts of the pan jus over the pork.
Boil macaroni until al dente, drain, and let cool.
Boil chicken breast, let it cool, and shred.
In a large bowl, mix macaroni, shredded chicken, mayonnaise, and condensed milk.
Add carrots, raisins, and cheese, and mix thoroughly.
Chill in the refrigerator before serving.
Sauté garlic, onion, and a generous amount of ginger in a pot.
Add chicken pieces and cook until the outer part turns light brown.
Pour water or chicken broth, bring to a boil, and simmer until the chicken is tender.
Add green papaya wedges and cook until tender, then stir in chili leaves or malunggay right before turning off the heat.
Boil water in a cooking pot.
Add pork face, ears, and salt. Boil for 45 minutes or until tender.
Drain the water and let the pork cool down.
Grill the pork face, ears, and liver until brown and slightly crisp.
Chop the grilled pork and liver into small pieces.
In a large bowl, combine the chopped meat with mayonnaise, vinegar, onion, ginger, and chili peppers.
Toss until well mixed. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Season fish with salt and pepper.
Fry the fish until golden brown. Set aside.
Heat oil in a pan. Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger.
Add bell peppers and carrots. Stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Pour in vinegar, water, sugar, and soy sauce. Let it boil.
Add cornstarch mixture to thicken the sauce.
Pour the sweet and sour sauce over the fried fish.
Sauté garlic, onion, and ginger in oil until fragrant.
Add chicken pieces and cook until outer part turns light brown.
Add glutinous rice and stir.
Pour water and bring to a boil.
Simmer, stirring occasionally, until rice is fully cooked and porridge reaches desired consistency.
Season with fish sauce and serve with boiled eggs and fried garlic.

Gather ingredients: 10-12 medium shrimp, peeled and deveined; 1 tablespoon minced garlic; 1 tablespoon minced ginger; 1 small onion, finely chopped; 1 medium tomato, diced; 1 cup coconut milk; 1 cup water; 2 tablespoons fish sauce; 1 teaspoon brown sugar; 1/2 teaspoon ground long pepper; 2 tablespoons cooking oil; fresh spring onions for garnish.
Heat the oil in a large heavy‑bottomed saucepan over medium heat until shimmering.
Add garlic, ginger, and onion. Sauté until aromatic and translucent, about 90 seconds.
Stir in diced tomato and cook until the tomato softens and releases some juice, about 120 seconds.
Pour in the coconut milk and water, then bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, just enough to avoid a rolling boil.
Let the coconut milk mixture simmer uncovered for 180 seconds (3 minutes) so it thickens slightly and the flavors marry.
Season with fish sauce, brown sugar, and long pepper. Stir until the sugar dissolves and the mixture tastes balanced.
Add the shrimp to the pan, reduce heat to low, and cover. Simmer until the shrimp turn pink and opaque, about 120 seconds.
Taste the sauce; adjust with more fish sauce or sugar if desired. If the sauce is too thick, add a splash of water.
Remove from heat and serve hot, garnished with sliced spring onions or fresh basil.
Clean the chicken pieces and pat them dry. Patience is key—don’t rush. The bones add flavor, so leave them in for a richer broth.

Heat 3 tablespoons of cooking oil in a wide, heavy‑sided pan over medium heat. When the oil shimmers, add 4 cloves of minced garlic, 1 teaspoon of minced ginger, and the finely sliced onion dippered on until the onion turns translucent and releases a fragrant aroma.
Add the chicken pieces to the pan, letting them brown on all sides. This caramelization locks in juices and gives the dish depth of flavor.
Pour in 1 cup of coconut milk and pour an additional 1 cup of water to create a creamy, slightly diluted broth. Stir gently to combine the coconut milk with the caramelized aromatics.
Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Add 2 bay leaves, a pinch of salt, and the fish sauce to taste. Swirl the pan to distribute the seasonings evenly.
Introduce the thickening agent: ½ cup of roasted coconut cream, which will enrich the sauce and give it that signature sago‑biscoit flavor.
Add halved carrots and sliced potatoes to the pan. These root vegetables absorb the coconut cream and create a comforting texture.
Drop in half a cup of sliced green beans and a handful of sliced eggplant. These vegetables add color and a slight earthiness that balances the richness of the coconut.
Cover the pan and let the stew cook on low heat until the chicken is tender and the vegetables are fork‑soft. Perform a gentle stir every 15 minutes to keep the ingredients from sticking.
Taste the broth and adjust seasonings: add a splash more fish sauce if it needs depth, a pinch of sugar to suit your palate, or a squeeze of calamansi juice for bright acidity.
Uncover the pot, turn off the heat, and let the dish sit for 2 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
Serve the ginataang manok hot over steamed white rice, garnishing with fresh cilantro, sliced green onions, and optionally a drizzle of hot chili oil for a kick.
Heat oil in a paellera or large pan.
Sauté garlic, onion, and bell peppers.
Add chicken and pork pieces. Cook until light brown.
Stir in the chorizo and raisins.
Add the glutinous and regular rice. Stir to combine with the ingredients.
Pour in chicken broth, tomato sauce, and coconut milk. Bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer until the rice is cooked and liquid is absorbed.
Garnish with boiled eggs and green peas before serving.
Heat oil in a wok.
Sauté garlic and onion.
Add chicken and pork, cook until brown.
Add soy sauce, oyster sauce, and chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Add cabbage and carrots, cook.
Remove vegetables and set aside. Add miki and bihon noodles to the broth.
Cook until liquid is absorbed.
Return vegetables, toss, and serve.
Rinse a cup of mung beans thoroughly, then soak them in a bowl covered with warm water for at least 5 hours (overnight if possible).
Drain the soaked mung beans and rinse them one more time; set aside.
Heat 2 tablespoons of cooking oil in a wok or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add 4 cloves of minced garlic and sauté for 1 minute until fragrant and golden brown.
Add ½ medium diced onion and cook for another minute until translucent.
Stir in 1 medium diced tomato and cook for 1 minute until the tomato softens.
Pour in 4 cups of water (or light fish stock for more depth) and bring the mixture to a rolling boil.
Add the drained mung beans to the pot, reduce heat to low, cover, and let the beans simmer until they reach desired tenderness (around 30 minutes).
If using fish fillets, add 2 medium fillets (tilapia, bangus, or sardines), then simmer for 5 minutes until the fish is cooked through.
Season the stew with 2 teaspoons of fish sauce (patis) or salt, 1 teaspoon of pepper, and a pinch of sugar to balance acidity.
Add sliced green onions and strew a handful of sliced fresh chilies if you like spice; stir and cook for 30 seconds just to warm them through.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Remove from heat, serve hot over steamed rice, and enjoy the comforting, savory flavors of Filipino mung bean stew.
Soak thick corn noodles in water, then boil until tender.
In a pan, make the sauce with shrimp juice, annatto water, and ground pork.
Thicken the sauce with cornstarch slurry and simmer.
Place cooked noodles on a plate and pour the orange sauce over them.
Garnish with crushed pork cracklings, boiled egg, and smoked fish flakes.
Sauté ginger, garlic, and onion in hot oil.
Add the chicken pieces and fish sauce, cooking until the chicken turns light brown.
Pour in rice washing or water. Let it boil and simmer until chicken is cooked.
Add cabbage and pechay, then cook briefly before serving.

recipes.name: Pork Adobo
recipes.description: A classic Filipino comfort dish where pork is braised in a savory mixture of soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, and bay leaves until it becomes tender and flavorful. The balance of saltiness, acidity, and subtle sweetness makes it a beloved staple, especially when paired with steaming hot rice.

instructions.text: Combine pork belly, soy sauce, and garlic in a bowl. Marinate for at least 1 hour.
Heat a cooking pot and add the marinated pork along with the marinade.
Let it boil and then simmer for 15 minutes.
Add water, whole peppercorns, and dried bay leaves. Simmer until the pork is tender.
Pour in vinegar. Let it boil for 5 minutes without stirring.
Add sugar and salt to taste. Simmer for a few more minutes until the sauce thickens.
